design.title: Dave's shoebox
design.brief:
Dave drives for gig apps and wants to replace his shoebox of receipts with a small database. Here is what he tracks.

Dave owns three VEHICLES: a car, a motor scooter, and a bicycle. For each vehicle he wants to record a vehicle ID (unique), a nickname, the type of vehicle, the model year, and an estimated cost per mile.

He works for several PLATFORMS (the gig apps). Each platform has a platform ID (unique), a name, a service type (rideshare, food delivery, or package delivery), and the commission percentage it takes.

Every shift is a GIG. A gig has a gig ID (unique), a date, the hours worked, the miles driven, the earnings, and the tips. Each gig is done on exactly one platform using exactly one vehicle. A platform may have many gigs (a new app may have none yet), and a vehicle may be used for many gigs or none. Dave would also like to see the net pay for each gig, which can be calculated from the earnings, the tips, and the platform's commission.

Dave also records EXPENSES. Each expense has an expense ID (unique), a date, an amount, and a note. Every expense belongs to exactly one EXPENSE CATEGORY (fuel, maintenance, insurance, phone, gear, parking); a category has many expenses or none. Most expenses are tied to exactly one vehicle, but some (like the phone plan) are not tied to any vehicle. A vehicle may have many expenses or none. An expense category has a category ID (unique) and a name.
hints: Five entities are written in capitals.
'Can be calculated' means a derived attribute; do not store it.
'Most expenses are tied to a vehicle, but some are not' means the VEHICLE side of that relationship is optional (minimum zero).
Every relationship here is 1:M; the foreign key always goes on the many side.

relationships.name: UsedFor
relationships.rationale: Each gig uses exactly one vehicle; a vehicle may be used for many gigs or none.

relationships.name: WorkedOn
relationships.rationale: Each gig is on exactly one platform; a platform may have many gigs or none.

relationships.name: Incurs
relationships.rationale: An expense is tied to at most one vehicle and sometimes none (optional on the vehicle side); a vehicle may have many expenses or none.

relationships.name: BelongsTo
relationships.rationale: Every expense has exactly one category; a category may have many expenses or none.

notes: NetPay is derived, so it is not a column. EXPENSE.VehicleID must allow NULL because the phone plan is not tied to a vehicle.

tests.sql: INSERT INTO VEHICLE (VehicleID, Nickname, VehicleType, ModelYear, CostPerMile) VALUES (1, 'The Corolla', 'Car', 2016, 0.32); INSERT INTO VEHICLE (VehicleID, Nickname, VehicleType, ModelYear, CostPerMile) VALUES (2, 'Vespa', 'Scooter', 2020, 0.11)

tests.description: A platform and a gig insert cleanly.
tests.sql: INSERT INTO PLATFORM (PlatformID, PlatformName, ServiceType, CommissionPct) VALUES (1, 'DashRush', 'Food delivery', 20); INSERT INTO GIG (GigID, GigDate, Hours, Miles, Earnings, Tips, PlatformID, VehicleID) VALUES (1, '2025-03-01', 4.5, 38.2, 71.5, 12.0, 1, 2)

tests.description: A gig on a platform that does not exist is rejected.
tests.sql: INSERT INTO GIG (GigID, GigDate, Hours, Miles, Earnings, Tips, PlatformID, VehicleID) VALUES (2, '2025-03-02', 3, 20, 50, 5, 99, 1)

tests.description: A phone-plan expense with no vehicle is allowed.
tests.sql: INSERT INTO EXPENSE_CATEGORY (CategoryID, CategoryName) VALUES (4, 'Phone'); INSERT INTO EXPENSE (ExpenseID, ExpenseDate, Amount, Note, VehicleID, CategoryID) VALUES (1, '2025-03-01', 45, 'Phone plan', NULL, 4)

tests.description: An expense in a category that does not exist is rejected.
tests.sql: INSERT INTO EXPENSE (ExpenseID, ExpenseDate, Amount, Note, VehicleID, CategoryID) VALUES (2, '2025-03-01', 30, 'Gas', 1, 42)

tests.description: A duplicate vehicle ID is rejected.
tests.sql: INSERT INTO VEHICLE (VehicleID, Nickname, VehicleType, ModelYear, CostPerMile) VALUES (1, 'Twin', 'Car', 2016, 0.3)

questions.text: List every column of every vehicle.
questions.sql: SELECT * FROM Vehicle

questions.text: List the name and commission percentage of every platform.
questions.sql: SELECT PlatformName, CommissionPct FROM Platform

questions.text: List the date, earnings and tips of every gig.
questions.sql: SELECT GigDate, Earnings, Tips FROM Gig

questions.text: List the gig ID and earnings of gigs that earned more than ${{amt}} (before tips).
questions.sql: SELECT GigID, Earnings FROM Gig WHERE Earnings > {{amt}}

questions.text: List the gig ID, date and hours of gigs done with vehicle {{vid}}.
questions.sql: SELECT GigID, GigDate, Hours FROM Gig WHERE VehicleID = {{vid}}

questions.text: List the gig ID and miles of gigs in {{month}} (YYYY-MM) with more than {{mi}} miles.
questions.sql: SELECT GigID, Miles FROM Gig WHERE GigMonth = '{{month}}' AND Miles > {{mi}}
hints: Two conditions joined with AND.

questions.text: List the distinct service types offered by the platforms.
questions.sql: SELECT DISTINCT ServiceType FROM Platform

questions.text: List every gig's ID and earnings, highest earnings first.
questions.sql: SELECT GigID, Earnings FROM Gig ORDER BY Earnings DESC

questions.text: List the expense ID, amount and note of expenses whose note contains '{{word}}'.
questions.sql: SELECT ExpenseID, Amount, Note FROM Expense WHERE Note LIKE '%{{word}}%'

questions.text: List the gig ID and hours of gigs lasting between {{lo}} and {{hi}} hours inclusive.
questions.sql: SELECT GigID, Hours FROM Gig WHERE Hours BETWEEN {{lo}} AND {{hi}}

questions.text: How many gigs has Dave logged in total? Return a single number.
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Gig

questions.text: What are Dave's total earnings and total tips across all gigs? Return both in one row.
questions.sql: SELECT SUM(Earnings), SUM(Tips) FROM Gig

questions.text: What is the total amount of expenses in {{month}} (YYYY-MM)? Return a single number.
questions.sql: SELECT SUM(Amount) FROM Expense WHERE ExpenseMonth = '{{month}}'

questions.text: What is the average earnings per gig on platform {{pid}}, rounded to 2 decimals? Return a single number.
questions.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(Earnings), 2) FROM Gig WHERE PlatformID = {{pid}}

questions.text: For each vehicle ID, show the vehicle ID and the number of gigs done with it.
questions.sql: SELECT VehicleID, COUNT(*) FROM Gig GROUP BY VehicleID

questions.text: For each platform ID, show the platform ID and total earnings (before tips).
questions.sql: SELECT PlatformID, SUM(Earnings) FROM Gig GROUP BY PlatformID

questions.text: Show total expenses per month: the month (YYYY-MM) and the sum of amounts, in chronological order.
questions.sql: SELECT ExpenseMonth, SUM(Amount) FROM Expense GROUP BY ExpenseMonth ORDER BY ExpenseMonth

questions.text: Show the months (YYYY-MM) in which Dave logged more than {{n}} gigs, with the count.
questions.sql: SELECT GigMonth, COUNT(*) FROM Gig GROUP BY GigMonth HAVING COUNT(*) > {{n}}
hints: A condition on COUNT(*) belongs in HAVING.

questions.text: List each gig's date and earnings together with the platform name.
questions.sql: SELECT G.GigDate, G.Earnings, P.PlatformName FROM Gig G JOIN Platform P ON G.PlatformID = P.PlatformID

questions.text: List the expense date, amount and category name for every expense in category '{{cat}}'.
questions.sql: SELECT E.ExpenseDate, E.Amount, C.CategoryName FROM Expense E JOIN ExpenseCategory C ON E.CategoryID = C.CategoryID WHERE C.CategoryName = '{{cat}}'

questions.text: For each vehicle nickname, show the nickname and the total miles driven on gigs.
questions.sql: SELECT V.Nickname, SUM(G.Miles) FROM Gig G JOIN Vehicle V ON G.VehicleID = V.VehicleID GROUP BY V.Nickname

questions.text: For each platform name, show the name and the average hours per gig, rounded to 2 decimals.
questions.sql: SELECT P.PlatformName, ROUND(AVG(G.Hours), 2) FROM Gig G JOIN Platform P ON G.PlatformID = P.PlatformID GROUP BY P.PlatformName

questions.text: For every gig, show the gig ID and the pay per hour (earnings plus tips, divided by hours), rounded to 2 decimals.
questions.sql: SELECT GigID, ROUND((Earnings + Tips) / Hours, 2) AS PayPerHour FROM Gig
hints: Arithmetic in the SELECT list; name the result with AS.

questions.text: For each vehicle nickname, show the nickname and the total expenses tied to that vehicle in category '{{cat}}'.
questions.sql: SELECT V.Nickname, SUM(E.Amount) FROM Expense E JOIN Vehicle V ON E.VehicleID = V.VehicleID JOIN ExpenseCategory C ON E.CategoryID = C.CategoryID WHERE C.CategoryName = '{{cat}}' GROUP BY V.Nickname

questions.text: List the expense ID, amount and note of expenses that are not tied to any vehicle.
questions.sql: SELECT ExpenseID, Amount, Note FROM Expense WHERE VehicleID IS NULL
hints: Use IS NULL.

questions.text: List the gig ID and earnings of gigs that earned more than the average gig earnings.
questions.sql: SELECT GigID, Earnings FROM Gig WHERE Earnings > (SELECT AVG(Earnings) FROM Gig)

questions.text: List the nicknames of vehicles that have no expenses recorded in category '{{cat}}'.
questions.sql: SELECT Nickname FROM Vehicle WHERE VehicleID NOT IN (SELECT VehicleID FROM Expense E JOIN ExpenseCategory C ON E.CategoryID = C.CategoryID WHERE C.CategoryName = '{{cat}}' AND VehicleID IS NOT NULL)
hints: NOT IN with a subquery; make sure the subquery does not return NULLs.

questions.text: List every platform name with the number of gigs done on it, including platforms with zero gigs.
questions.sql: SELECT P.PlatformName, COUNT(G.GigID) FROM Platform P LEFT JOIN Gig G ON P.PlatformID = G.PlatformID GROUP BY P.PlatformID, P.PlatformName
hints: LEFT JOIN from Platform; COUNT a Gig column so empty platforms show 0.

questions.text: For each service type, show the service type and total tips earned.
questions.sql: SELECT P.ServiceType, SUM(G.Tips) FROM Gig G JOIN Platform P ON G.PlatformID = P.PlatformID GROUP BY P.ServiceType

questions.text: Show the vehicle IDs whose gigs have earned more than ${{amt}} in total (earnings only), with the total.
questions.sql: SELECT VehicleID, SUM(Earnings) FROM Gig GROUP BY VehicleID HAVING SUM(Earnings) > {{amt}}

presentation.title: How much did I make?
presentation.brief: Dave asks: "Just tell me one number: how much did I earn in total, before tips?" Build a visual that shows exactly that.
hints: A card shows a single value.
Earnings lives in the Gig table.

presentation.title: Which app pays best?
presentation.brief: Dave wants to compare the apps: total earnings for each platform name, biggest first, with a title he can screenshot.
hints: Platform names are categories: bars or columns.
Sort by value, descending.
presentation.referenceSql: SELECT P.PlatformName, SUM(G.Earnings) FROM Gig G JOIN Platform P ON G.PlatformID = P.PlatformID GROUP BY P.PlatformName ORDER BY 2 DESC

presentation.title: Is it getting better?
presentation.brief: Dave wants to see how his monthly earnings (before tips) changed over 2025, month by month in order, with a title.
hints: Months in order call for a line chart.
GigMonth is already stored as YYYY-MM.
presentation.referenceSql: SELECT GigMonth, SUM(Earnings) FROM Gig GROUP BY GigMonth ORDER BY 1

presentation.title: Where does the money go?
presentation.brief: Dave asks what share of his expenses goes to each category (by category name), as parts of a whole. Add a title.
hints: Six categories: a pie or donut is acceptable here.
Sum the Amount column.
presentation.referenceSql: SELECT C.CategoryName, SUM(E.Amount) FROM Expense E JOIN ExpenseCategory C ON E.CategoryID = C.CategoryID GROUP BY C.CategoryName ORDER BY 2 DESC

presentation.title: What does the car cost me?
presentation.brief: Dave suspects the car is expensive. Show his monthly expenses (by ExpenseMonth, in order) for the vehicle nicknamed 'The Corolla' only, with a title.
hints: Filter on the vehicle's Nickname rather than on an ID.
Months in order: a line, or columns if you prefer.
presentation.referenceSql: SELECT E.ExpenseMonth, SUM(E.Amount) FROM Expense E JOIN Vehicle V ON E.VehicleID = V.VehicleID WHERE V.Nickname = 'The Corolla' GROUP BY E.ExpenseMonth ORDER BY 1

presentation.title: Miles per vehicle
presentation.brief: Dave wants exact numbers in a table: each vehicle nickname, its vehicle type, and the total miles driven on gigs, most miles first.
hints: Table visual; leave Nickname and VehicleType unsummarized.
Sort by the value.
presentation.referenceSql: SELECT V.Nickname, V.VehicleType, SUM(G.Miles) FROM Gig G JOIN Vehicle V ON G.VehicleID = V.VehicleID GROUP BY V.Nickname, V.VehicleType ORDER BY 3 DESC

questions.text: Show one number: total earnings (before tips) across all of Dave's gigs.
questions.sql: SELECT SUM(Earnings) FROM Gig
hints: A card shows a single value.
Earnings lives in Gig.

questions.text: Show one number: how many gigs Dave has worked.
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(GigID) FROM Gig
hints: Count the gig IDs.

questions.text: Show one number: the total tips Dave has received.
questions.sql: SELECT SUM(Tips) FROM Gig

questions.text: Show one number: the biggest single-gig earnings (before tips).
questions.sql: SELECT MAX(Earnings) FROM Gig
hints: Change the aggregation on the value.

questions.text: Compare total earnings (before tips) across the platforms, by platform name.
questions.sql: SELECT P.PlatformName, SUM(G.Earnings) FROM Gig G JOIN Platform P ON G.PlatformID = P.PlatformID GROUP BY P.PlatformName
hints: Axis: PlatformName; values: sum of Earnings. The join is automatic.

questions.text: Compare total miles driven per vehicle, by nickname.
questions.sql: SELECT V.Nickname, SUM(G.Miles) FROM Gig G JOIN Vehicle V ON G.VehicleID = V.VehicleID GROUP BY V.Nickname

questions.text: Compare the average hours per gig on each platform (by name).
questions.sql: SELECT P.PlatformName, AVG(G.Hours) FROM Gig G JOIN Platform P ON G.PlatformID = P.PlatformID GROUP BY P.PlatformName
hints: Average, not sum.

questions.text: Compare the number of gigs done with each vehicle type.
questions.sql: SELECT V.VehicleType, COUNT(G.GigID) FROM Gig G JOIN Vehicle V ON G.VehicleID = V.VehicleID GROUP BY V.VehicleType

questions.text: Compare the number of expenses recorded in each expense category (by name).
questions.sql: SELECT C.CategoryName, COUNT(E.ExpenseID) FROM Expense E JOIN ExpenseCategory C ON E.CategoryID = C.CategoryID GROUP BY C.CategoryName

questions.text: Show how total earnings (before tips) changed month by month. Use GigMonth.
questions.sql: SELECT GigMonth, SUM(Earnings) FROM Gig GROUP BY GigMonth
hints: A trend over time wants a line.

questions.text: Show the monthly total of expenses over time (ExpenseMonth).
questions.sql: SELECT ExpenseMonth, SUM(Amount) FROM Expense GROUP BY ExpenseMonth

questions.text: A titled line chart of total miles per month (GigMonth). Give it a title.
questions.sql: SELECT GigMonth, SUM(Miles) FROM Gig GROUP BY GigMonth

questions.text: Show each expense category's share of the total amount spent (by category name).
questions.sql: SELECT C.CategoryName, SUM(E.Amount) FROM Expense E JOIN ExpenseCategory C ON E.CategoryID = C.CategoryID GROUP BY C.CategoryName
hints: Six categories or fewer: a pie is fine; bars work too.

questions.text: Show how the number of gigs splits across service types (rideshare, food, package).
questions.sql: SELECT P.ServiceType, COUNT(G.GigID) FROM Gig G JOIN Platform P ON G.PlatformID = P.PlatformID GROUP BY P.ServiceType

questions.text: A table listing every vehicle: nickname, vehicle type and model year.
questions.sql: SELECT Nickname, VehicleType, ModelYear FROM Vehicle
hints: Three columns, no aggregation needed (one row per vehicle).

questions.text: A table with one row per platform: platform name, total earnings and total tips.
questions.sql: SELECT P.PlatformName, SUM(G.Earnings), SUM(G.Tips) FROM Gig G JOIN Platform P ON G.PlatformID = P.PlatformID GROUP BY P.PlatformName

questions.text: Monthly total earnings (GigMonth), but only for gigs on {{platform}}.
questions.sql: SELECT G.GigMonth, SUM(G.Earnings) FROM Gig G JOIN Platform P ON G.PlatformID = P.PlatformID WHERE P.PlatformName = '{{platform}}' GROUP BY G.GigMonth
hints: Drop PlatformName into the filters and tick one value.

questions.text: Total expense amount by category name, counting only expenses tied to {{vehicle}}.
questions.sql: SELECT C.CategoryName, SUM(E.Amount) FROM Expense E JOIN ExpenseCategory C ON E.CategoryID = C.CategoryID JOIN Vehicle V ON E.VehicleID = V.VehicleID WHERE V.Nickname = '{{vehicle}}' GROUP BY C.CategoryName

questions.text: Number of gigs per platform name, counting only gigs of at least {{h}} hours.
questions.sql: SELECT P.PlatformName, COUNT(G.GigID) FROM Gig G JOIN Platform P ON G.PlatformID = P.PlatformID WHERE G.Hours >= {{h}} GROUP BY P.PlatformName
hints: A numeric filter is a range: from the threshold up to something huge.

questions.text: Total pay including tips, per platform name. Define a calculated field: Earnings + Tips.
questions.sql: SELECT P.PlatformName, SUM(G.Earnings + G.Tips) FROM Gig G JOIN Platform P ON G.PlatformID = P.PlatformID GROUP BY P.PlatformName
hints: Create the field, then sum it on the y-axis.

questions.text: Earnings per hour by vehicle nickname, computed as total earnings divided by total hours: SUM(Earnings) / SUM(Hours).
questions.sql: SELECT V.Nickname, SUM(G.Earnings) / SUM(G.Hours) FROM Gig G JOIN Vehicle V ON G.VehicleID = V.VehicleID GROUP BY V.Nickname
hints: This is an aggregate measure: write the SUMs inside the calculated field.

questions.text: Net pay after commission per platform name: sum of Earnings * (1 - CommissionPct / 100.0).
questions.sql: SELECT P.PlatformName, SUM(G.Earnings * (1 - P.CommissionPct / 100.0)) FROM Gig G JOIN Platform P ON G.PlatformID = P.PlatformID GROUP BY P.PlatformName
hints: The expression mixes two tables; the builder joins them for you.

questions.text: Total miles per vehicle type, broken down by platform name (one series per platform).
questions.sql: SELECT V.VehicleType, P.PlatformName, SUM(G.Miles) FROM Gig G JOIN Vehicle V ON G.VehicleID = V.VehicleID JOIN Platform P ON G.PlatformID = P.PlatformID GROUP BY V.VehicleType, P.PlatformName
hints: Axis: VehicleType; legend: PlatformName.

questions.text: Total expense amount per category name, split by vehicle type.
questions.sql: SELECT C.CategoryName, V.VehicleType, SUM(E.Amount) FROM Expense E JOIN ExpenseCategory C ON E.CategoryID = C.CategoryID JOIN Vehicle V ON E.VehicleID = V.VehicleID GROUP BY C.CategoryName, V.VehicleType

questions.text: Rank the platforms by total tips, highest first (bar chart, sorted).
questions.sql: SELECT P.PlatformName, SUM(G.Tips) FROM Gig G JOIN Platform P ON G.PlatformID = P.PlatformID GROUP BY P.PlatformName ORDER BY 2 DESC

questions.text: Vehicles (by nickname) ordered by total expense amount, LOWEST first.
questions.sql: SELECT V.Nickname, SUM(E.Amount) FROM Expense E JOIN Vehicle V ON E.VehicleID = V.VehicleID GROUP BY V.Nickname ORDER BY 2 ASC
hints: Bars default to descending; change the sort.
